title: The Last Contact
premise: Coral Coldharbour, a veteran air-crash investigator haunted by the row-twelve deaths of her family, has spent a decade hiding inside procedure and paperwork. When a stranger named Ivo Kessler repays a favor she never performed—and demands interest in the form of her silence about a falsified maintenance log tied to Flight 4471—Coral realizes the crash that killed her family was no accident. Pulled into an underground network of investigators who deliver justice the law cannot, she must decide whether to expose the truth or trade it away. In the end, Coral leaks the secret minutes before Frankfurt's markets open, collapsing the airline's parent company and finally claiming belonging among the living rather than the dead.
about_author: Freya Nystrom is a former aviation insurance analyst who spent eight years reading black-box transcripts before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Jutland coast, where the fog does most of the editing.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Ten years after the crash, Coral works a routine runway incursion case in Reykjavik, methodical and invisible. A delayed flight forces her past the memorial wall, where she touches row twelve's names. Emotional beat: grief managed like evidence—catalogued, sealed, never opened.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Was
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A stranger, Ivo Kessler, appears at her hotel bar and thanks her for saving his sister's visa appeal—a favor she never did. He leaves an envelope: photos of a maintenance log she recognizes. Beat: unease curdling into recognition; her anonymity has been breached.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo explains the debt structure: someone paid Coral's family settlement early and quietly, and now the payer wants discretion about Flight 4471's tail-fin inspection. Coral refuses. Beat: the trap revealed—her silence was purchased years ago without her knowledge.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She pulls archived records and finds her own signature on a document dated while she was hospitalized. Someone has been wearing her identity for a decade. Beat: vertigo—the investigator discovers she is the investigated.

chapters.title: The Ninth Floor
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Her supervisor, Brandt, warns her off, then slips her a keycard to a sealed archive. She finds Flight 4471's original inspection report—altered. Beat: first proof; fear becomes purpose.

chapters.title: Kessler's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo reveals he belongs to the Meridian Circle, an extralegal network of investigators who settle what courts cannot. He offers Coral membership—if she delivers the unaltered log before Frankfurt opens Monday. Beat: temptation framed as inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Dead Sign
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She visits her brother's widow, Lena, who admits accepting the mysterious settlement. Guilt surfaces on both sides. Beat: belonging tested by complicity; family wounds reopened under new light.

chapters.title: Tail Number 4471
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Reconstructing the flight path, Coral matches the falsified inspection to a hydraulic failure timeline—row twelve took the impact because the crew fought a failure they were told couldn't happen. Beat: cold fury; the rules she served were the murder weapon.

chapters.title: Brandt's Silence
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt confesses he buried the report to protect his pension and his son's medical debts. He begs Coral to let it stay buried. Beat: sympathy for the compromised man; justice shown to be expensive for everyone.

chapters.title: The Watcher in Departures
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Someone photographs her at the airport; her apartment is searched but nothing taken—except her father's watch. The message is clear: they can reach her history itself. Beat: paranoia tightens; stakes become personal property of memory.

chapters.title: Meridian Rules
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At a safehouse, the Circle debates whether Coral is an asset or a leak. Ivo vouches for her; a rival member, Sable, votes against. Beat: Coral glimpses the community she craves—and its capacity for ruthlessness.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral receives two envelopes: one from the airline's fixer offering money and erasure of her past, one from the Circle offering truth and no protection. Beat: the choice crystallized; belonging versus safety.

chapters.title: Lena's Testimony
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Lena reveals the settlement came with a condition: never ask questions. She kept the letter. Inside is a name—Aurelia Voss, the airline's chairwoman and the person who signed Coral's forged signature. Beat: the antagonist acquires a face.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Aurelia Voss reviews the Coldharbour file with surgical calm, ordering the 'interest' collected before markets open. She believes stability justifies sacrifice. Beat: chilling competence; the reader understands the machine's logic.

chapters.title: The Copy House
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. With Brandt's keycard, Coral copies the original log in a basement records facility as alarms trigger. She escapes through loading docks, chased by corporate security. Beat: action peak one; she commits fully to the crime of truth.

chapters.title: Sable's Price
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable intercepts Coral, offering to sell her to Voss unless she hands over the log. Coral negotiates: the Circle gets the copy, she keeps the original. Beat: trust brokered at knifepoint; alliances revealed as transactions.

chapters.title: Friday Night, Frankfurt
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral and Ivo reach Frankfurt, planning to release the log to regulators and press simultaneously at market open. Ivo confesses his sister died on 4471 too—the favor story was bait to reach Coral. Beat: betrayal and kinship fused; two mourners, one debt.

chapters.title: The Offered Trade
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Voss meets Coral privately: the original log for the full truth about who ordered the forgery—including the name of the investigator who helped, years ago, to protect Coral herself. Beat: climax of moral weight; the secret worth killing for turns out to implicate her savior.

chapters.title: Market Open
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs intercut. At 9:00 a.m., Coral releases everything—the log, the forgery, Voss's signature chain. Markets crater; Voss is detained mid-broadcast. Beat: catharsis through exposure; justice arrives not by verdict but by daylight.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Hearings begin; Brandt testifies and loses everything but his son. The Circle dissolves its claim on Coral—membership declined. Beat: quiet reckoning; she chooses open grief over secret belonging.

chapters.title: Returning the Watch
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral tracks down the man who took her father's watch—a former Circle courier acting on old orders—and takes it back without anger. She visits row twelve and reads the names aloud, all of them. Beat: mourning completed; inheritance reclaimed as memory, not money.

chapters.title: The Next Contact
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue. Months later, Coral trains new investigators, teaching them to read what files hide. An envelope arrives: another favor that never happened, another debt. She smiles, pockets it, and boards the plane. Beat: cyclical ending—belonging found in vigilance; the story's engine restarts.
